observations.epoch_band_state_and_other_notes: WD+M-dwarf interpretation is favored by the optical composite-spectrum model; the WD itself is not directly resolved spectroscopically, and magnetic/polar status is unconfirmed. Hurley-Walker+24 detected 30–60 s recurring pulses at 10496.5522 +/- 0.0008 s in MWA 72–231 MHz/MeerKAT UHF 550–1050 MHz; 3-sigma persistent UHF limit <30 uJy/beam outside pulses. Rodriguez+25 Keck Na I RVs give Porb=10496 +/- 5 s, nearly matching the radio recurrence; this is not a measured WD spin. The ~6.27 yr timing term may be timing noise or another orbit. Catalog distance retains Rodriguez+25/+26 composite SED fit 380 +/- 10 pc; competing DM, Gaia/Bailer-Jones, and discovery 1.5 +/- 0.5 kpc values remain separate in the measurement ledger and GLEAM0704-001. XMM reports unabsorbed 0.3–10 keV upper limits only; the main fixed-band X-ray flux cells remain NA. See [local artifact withheld]

issues.competing_evidence: Rodriguez+25/+26 composite SED fit 380±10 pc; discovery YMW16 0.4±0.1 kpc and NE2001 1.8±0.5 kpc then adopted 1.5±0.5 kpc; exact Gaia DR3 parallax −0.223±0.981 mas yields Bailer-Jones geometric 3.010 [1.566,6.045] kpc and photogeometric 3.859 [3.273,4.252] kpc. Rodriguez+25 Appendix E.1 prints 3.9(+3.0/−1.5) kpc, whose center resembles photogeometric but interval resembles geometric.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance controls luminosities and absolute magnitude; the poor/negative parallax is not a direct distance, and the exact Bailer-Jones row does not unambiguously reproduce the appendix notation.
issues.needed_action: Decide whether 380 pc remains the compatibility display as a model-dependent SED distance while all alternatives are shown, and verify which Bailer-Jones posterior Rodriguez+25 intended (or whether its text is a typo). Do not average the methods.

issues.competing_evidence: M-dwarf RV orbit and blue continuum favor a compact WD; Rodriguez+25/+26 fit a DA WD+M model and argue against an NS, but no WD Balmer/Zeeman/cyclotron signature or WD field is directly measured. Radio coherency motivates magnetism but does not measure it.
issues.why_it_matters: A confirmed-WD versus WD-favored label affects RAWDOG population counts and comparison with magnetic CVs/WD pulsars.
issues.needed_action: Choose whether the WD+M composite-spectrum inference qualifies for the confirmed-WD sample, or should remain a favored/inferred WD classification pending direct WD evidence; retain magnetic/polar status as unconfirmed meanwhile.

issues.parameter: radio recurrence, orbit, spin and long timing term
issues.competing_evidence: Radio recurrence 10496.5522±0.0008 s; two-night RV orbit 10496±5 s (one-night 10500±500 s). The ~6.27±0.23 yr sinusoid with 60.5±11.2 light-second projected amplitude may be timing noise or orbital/super-orbital motion. The fitted radio Pdot includes zero; 3σ upper limit <3.9e−11 s/s.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating radio recurrence as WD spin or the long sinusoid as an orbit would change magnetic/synchronization and evolutionary interpretation.
issues.needed_action: Keep recurrence and RV orbit as separate measurements; decide only after phase-connected timing clarifies the long-term residuals whether any spin or additional orbit is supported.

issues.parameter: SED component values and reddening assumptions
issues.competing_evidence: WD/donor temperatures, radii, WD mass, distance, q, inclination and filling factor come from a composite MCMC model: DA Koester log g=8, BT-DUSTY solar log g=5, 10-Gyr Baraffe donor, imposed 10% radius inflation, and E(B−V) tied to Edenhofer dust map. A fixed E(B−V)=0.3 branch lowers the fitted WD mass from 1.02 to 0.82 M_sun.
issues.why_it_matters: These are model-dependent component estimates, not independent dynamical measurements or Gaia single-star parameters.
issues.needed_action: Keep each quantity tagged as an SED/model result with the assumptions and alternative extinction branch; decide whether the data-dictionary category should call these inferred rather than measured component properties.

issues.competing_evidence: Rodriguez+25 finds weak H-alpha with a possible ~330 km/s component outside the M dwarf, but only one orbit of spectra was available and chromospheric activity remains an alternative; Rodriguez+26 retains the need for follow-up.
issues.why_it_matters: The line origin bears on accretion state and whether the radio source is interacting through a compact-object magnetosphere.
issues.needed_action: Obtain multi-epoch phase-resolved H-alpha spectroscopy; leave accretion or magnetic-channeling interpretation unresolved.
